title: The dog's summer
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The dog has had a summer: the bay, the mill, the tourists, the chair's shadow to lie in. Wood draws him asleep on the dock at the end of August and counts the things he's learned. Eleven. The uncle counted the swims. Same number. Nobody planned it.

panels.composition: The dock, evening. BARNABY asleep on the planks, the ammonite ball, the kelp line faint. WOOD drawing. The UNCLE in the chair.

image.prompt: a small dog curled tightly asleep on a dock's planks at evening with a faint wavy line rising from its coat, a young man drawing and an old man in a lawn chair nearby, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pad: the dog, and beside him a list in the margin, small, eleven lines as blocks.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with a sleeping dog and a short list of eleven lines in the margin rendered as blocks, black and white, no words
an old man in a lawn chair, flat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dock. The dog. The two of them. The bay. The end of August drawn as a dog asleep. The strip finds that's enough.

notes: 'Nobody plans the good ones.' Eleven, twice.
